memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country of Gilead when Laban overtook him, and Laban and his relatives camped there too. Then Laban said to Jacob, 'What have you done? You've deceived me, and you've carried off my daughters like captives in war. Why did you run off secretly and deceive me? Why didn't you tell me, so I could send you away with joy and singing to the music of timbrels and harps? You didn't even let me kiss my grandchildren and my daughters goodbye. You have done a foolish thing. I have the power to harm you; but last night the God of your father said to me, "Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad." Now you have gone off because you longed to return to your father's household. But why did you steal my gods?'" - Gen 31:25-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Laban confronts Jacob with a long list of grievances. Some even sound reasonable — he was not given the chance to say goodbye to his daughters and grandchildren. Yet his words are a strange mixture. He paints himself as the wounded party who only wanted a joyful farewell, conveniently forgetting his years of cheating Jacob. And he lets slip, "I have the power to harm you" — revealing that his intentions were not so innocent after all.

But then Laban admits the one thing that changed everything: "last night the God of your father said to me..." God's warning had stopped him in his tracks. For all his bluster and power, Laban was held back by the God of Jacob.

Notice his last complaint: "Why did you steal my gods?" Laban is distraught over stolen idols — small figures that had to be carried, that could be taken by someone else. There is a quiet irony here. A "god" that can be stolen is no god at all. Laban trusted in helpless idols, while Jacob was protected by the living God who commands even dreams.

This searches our hearts. Where do we place our trust — in "gods" we must protect and carry, or in the God who protects and carries us? Only the living God is worthy of our full trust.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I quick to see others' faults while excusing my own, as Laban did?
2. Where do I trust in "gods" I must protect, rather than the God who protects me?
3. How does it comfort me that God can restrain even those with power to harm?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are the living God who protects and carries Your people. Keep me from trusting in helpless idols, and help me to place my full confidence in You alone. Amen.
